paper_title: A computational search for the optimal microelectronic heat sink using ANSYS Icepak

extraction.paper_title: A computational search for the optimal microelectronic heat sink using ANSYS Icepak

scenario.description: Steady 3D ANSYS Icepak (FLUENT solver) simulation of the inline-arrangement (IA) circular pin-fin aluminium heat sink with 36 fins. The source temperature is reported as 126.97 C (Table 6). The packet shows no code, config or data links; the Data availability statement says no data was used. The paper gives conflicting heat sink and fin dimensions: Table 1 says 4x4x1.7 cm with D=0.2 cm, while the text says 3x3.5x2 cm with fin radius 0.16 cm and height 1.5 cm. Chip position coordinates are not given.
scenario.architecture: Single chip 2.2 x 2.2 x 0.1 cm on a substrate board, with an aluminium pin-fin heat sink (36 inline circular fins) in a 6 x 5 x 2 cm cabinet. Air-cooled, with adiabatic walls except the inlet and outlet.
scenario.workload: Constant uniform 8 W heat load on the chip. No application workload is specified.
scenario.operating_point: Inlet velocity 0.1 m/s, inlet air temperature 298 K, power 8 W, steady state, realizable k-epsilon turbulence model.

original_setup.solver: ANSYS Icepak (FLUENT solver), 3D steady-state, pressure-based, implicit, realizable k-epsilon turbulence with standard wall functions; conjugate conduction plus forced-air convection (Table 2, pdf pages 3 and 5-6)
original_setup.optimizer: None. The paper compares four fixed geometries (inline/staggered x circular/conical fins) by parametric comparison. No optimization algorithm is used.
original_setup.controller: None. There is no thermal controller or DVFS; the chip heat load is constant at 8 W.
original_setup.benchmark: Validated against the Adhikari et al. experiment (Fig. 6, deviation under 3.68%) and the Rosli et al. numerical study (Table 5: IA 107.43 C vs 106.474 C, SA 101.85 C vs 101.662 C). The selected scenario is the inline circular pin-fin heat sink (Table 6, pdf page 11).

thermal_observable.location: Heat source (chip) maximum temperature for the inline (IA) circular pin-fin case. Section 2.1 defines delta T_max as the maximum temperature on the fin base minus the ambient air temperature, so the exact location is ambiguous.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Maximum (peak) steady-state source temperature from the 3D CFD solution

physical_mismatches.reason: The original model is a 3D forced-air convection CFD case (inlet velocity 0.1 m/s, realizable k-epsilon, pressure outlet) with a pin-fin heat sink in a cabinet. A steady 2D conduction floorplan model cannot represent the fluid flow, pressure drop, or 36 discrete pin fins.

The cooling path is an air-cooled finned heat sink with a velocity inlet and pressure outlet. A Studio package/heat-sink model would have to replace this with an effective convection coefficient or boundary resistance, which changes the thermal result.

The paper gives conflicting heat sink and fin dimensions. Table 1 says heat sink 4x4x1.7 cm and fin D=0.2 cm. The text says 3x3.5x2 cm, fin radius 0.16 cm and height 1.5 cm. Chip coordinates are not given. A consistent geometry cannot be built from the paper alone.

The paper has no optimizer or controller, no transient behaviour, and no reliability analysis. Optimizer, controller, transient, and reliability comparisons are therefore not applicable to this scenario.

There is no 3D stack or interposer. The paper has a single chip on a substrate board and a heat sink with an adiabatic cabinet except at the inlet and outlet. Substrate and chip layer properties are not given.

The solver assumptions are internally inconsistent: Table 2 says 'Axisymmetric' and the text lists 'laminar flow' alongside a k-epsilon turbulence model. The inlet temperature is 298 K in Table 3 but about 295 K in the Fig. 9 text. The validation case in Table 5 (IA 106.474 C, 0.4 cm gap) differs from the selected case value (126.97 C).

methods.note: The 3D steady Icepak/FLUENT, realizable k-epsilon setup is stated on pdf pages 3 and 5-7. The paper contradicts itself on the flow regime: Table 2 says 'Axisymmetric' and the assumptions list says 'Laminar flow', while the model is a 3D k-epsilon case. The extraction records this as a non-essential mismatch, but it means the solver description is not a consistent method. The case is 3D forced-air CFD, so it is not a 2D reproduction.

code.note: The packet lists no assets and the Data availability statement (pdf page 11) says no data was used. There is no code, repository, Icepak project or geometry file to verify. The extraction's checked_no_links status matches this, but nothing can be reproduced from code.

parameters.note: The chip size (2.2 x 2.2 x 0.1 cm), 8 W, 0.1 m/s, 298 K and 36 fins match Tables 1 and 3. The heat sink is 4x4x1.7 cm in Table 1 but 3x3.5x2 cm in the text. The fin is D=0.2 cm in Table 1 but radius 0.16 cm and height 1.5 cm in the text. The base height is 0.2 cm in Table 1 against a 2 cm third dimension in the text. Tin is 298 K in Table 3 but 295 K in the Fig. 9 discussion. Fin pitch, cabinet axis assignment and material properties are not given. No self-consistent parameter set exists.

config.note: The extraction's experiment has an empty floorplan and empty power_w, and the chip x/y position is null. The packet has no coordinates for the chip or heat sink, no block geometry file and no Studio configuration, so no same-scenario power-per-block mapping can be checked. The extraction claims Fig. 1 (c,d) has no coordinates, but only pdftotext output is in the packet, so that figure was not visually inspected.

data.note: The text-table values (Table 6: 126.97 C for IA circular, Table 3, Table 4, Table 5) are present in the extracted text. The decisive figures (Fig. 1, Figs. 6-12) are not supplied as images, so no digitization or visual verification was possible. The Rth value is not tabulated and there are no raw data. The Table 7 pressure drop has no unit. The temperature location is ambiguous: 'Source' in Table 6 versus 'fin base' in Eq. 8.

findings.reason: The experiment is labelled custom_2d_steady with an empty floorplan and empty power map, while the scenario is a 3D forced-air pin-fin CFD case and steady_2d_relevant is false. The label implies a 2D reproduction that the evidence does not support. The decisive 3D, airflow and pin-fin features cannot be reduced to 2D without invented effective boundary conditions.

The chip coordinates are null, so no floorplan block can be placed and per-block power cannot be tied to geometry. The assertion that Fig. 1 has no coordinates was not visually verified because no figure image is in the packet.

The paper contradicts itself (4x4x1.7 cm against 3x3.5x2 cm). The extraction records only the first value of each triplet, so the evidence rows are incomplete. The base height of 0.2 cm and the text's 2 cm are also inconsistent. No decisive geometry can be approved.

assessment.summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable, and Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped). The gate failed because the custom 2D steady experiment has no floorplan blocks and no power_w object, so input validity failed. The evidence entries also lack valid page or pinned-asset locators, and the adversarial and independent reviews are unresolved. The scenario is a steady 3D Icepak/FLUENT forced-air CFD case: an inline 36-pin circular-fin aluminium heat sink, an 8 W chip, 0.1 m/s inlet air at 298 K, and a reported source temperature of 126.97 C in Table 6. A steady 2D conduction floorplan model cannot represent the airflow, pressure drop or discrete pin fins. Representing the air-cooled heat sink would need an effective convection coefficient that the paper does not provide. The gate set comparison_valid to false, and there is no Studio output, so no numeric comparison with 126.97 C is made, and no replication or agreement is claimed. This custom steady run would in any case have no transient trace. The paper has no optimizer, controller, transient or reliability results, so none of those comparisons apply. Qualitatively, the paper's conclusions depend on fin arrangement, fin shape and airflow, which a 2D conduction screen cannot test. The paper's validation cases (Adhikari 3.68% deviation, Rosli IA 106.474 vs 107.43 C) are separate geometries and must not be mixed with the 126.97 C value.
limitations: Studio was not run, so there is no simulated temperature, and no numeric comparison is made. comparison_valid is false.
The custom 2D steady experiment has no floorplan blocks or power_w mapping, which fails the input-validity gate.

The source is a 3D conjugate CFD case with forced-air convection, a k-epsilon turbulence model and 36 discrete pin fins, so a 2D conduction model would need an unpublished effective convection coefficient.

The paper's heat sink and fin dimensions conflict: Table 1 gives 4x4x1.7 cm with D=0.2 cm, while the text gives 3x3.5x2 cm with radius 0.16 cm and height 1.5 cm. The chip coordinates and fin pitch are missing.
The 126.97 C observable has an ambiguous location (chip source vs fin base, per the Eq. 8 definition) and no stated spatial aggregation beyond a maximum. Only the steady regime is relevant.

No linked code, data, config or geometry assets exist, and the Data availability statement says no data was used. Chip, substrate and interface material properties and contact resistance are not given.
The inlet temperature is inconsistent in the paper (298 K in Table 3 vs about 295 K in the text). The solver description is also inconsistent (axisymmetric, laminar and turbulent are all mentioned).
The paper's validation cases use different geometries and values (Table 5, Adhikari rectangular fins) from the selected scenario and are not comparable with it.
The adversarial checks (methods, code, parameters, config, data) and the independent page/asset review are unresolved, so the extracted evidence is unverified.
The optimizer, controller, transient and reliability comparisons are not applicable, because the paper compares four fixed geometries and has no such components.
